bonding: They have to do a small task together that requires quiet coordination.
One of them shows up with something mundane they remembered the other likes.
They share a space neither of them chose, and it feels unexpectedly safe.
confession: They start to say the truth, then pivot, then try again.
A confession arrives sideways, wrapped in a story that is not quite a story.
They admit something small that implies something much bigger.
grief: Grief shows up as irritation first, then silence.
They try to fix something trivial because the real loss can’t be fixed.
A memory interrupts the present at the worst possible moment.
suspense: A message arrives too late to stop what’s already in motion.
Someone realizes they’re being watched, but can’t prove it.
The room goes quiet for no clear reason, and it stays quiet.
filler: They run an errand that becomes more intimate than expected.
A small delay forces them to sit together without distraction.
They do something routine while avoiding what they actually want to say.
